measure: Price of inelastic physical endowments relative to manufactured goods: an index of urban residential land values (or the land share of home values) and of water rights and critical minerals, divided by the consumer price index for manufactured goods.
public_sources: National statistics on land and house prices; consumer price indices by category; commodity price series.
counts_against: In most of the large economies examined, the ratio is lower at the final reading than at the 2026 baseline: inelastic endowments became cheaper relative to manufactured goods while AI deployment scaled.
does_not_count: A fall in one commodity or one city. The prediction is about the composition of physical rents, so a broad measure is needed.

measure: Operating margin and return on invested capital of infrastructure owners, aggregated by group: leading-edge chip foundries, the cloud segments of hyperscale providers, large data-center operators. Recorded with it: lead times for new capacity (fab construction, grid connection of a data center).
public_sources: Company annual reports and segment disclosures; energy agency and grid operator reports on connection queues.
counts_against: The aggregate operating margin of these groups is lower at the final reading than at the 2026 baseline although lead times for new capacity have not shortened: rents were competed away while the bottleneck was still in place.
does_not_count: A fall in margins after capacity expanded quickly. The article's prediction carries the qualifier 'unless capacity expands quickly', so in that case it is untested, not refuted. Each reading must therefore state whether lead times shortened and how much capacity was added.

measure: Ratio of pay in frontier roles to pay in routine, codifiable roles within the same field: for example system design, integration, evaluation and safety against routine programming, standard content production and basic analysis.
public_sources: Occupational wage statistics of national statistical offices; published salary surveys.
counts_against: The ratio is lower at the final reading than at the 2026 baseline: pay for routine, codifiable work held up or rose relative to frontier work.
does_not_count: A fall in employment alone. The prediction is about rents, so it is read in pay, not in headcount.

measure: For rule-gated essentials (housing supply, clinical deployment of AI, autonomous transport): entry and household prices compared across jurisdictions with similar AI adoption and different rules, and across jurisdictions with similar rules and different AI adoption.
public_sources: Housing permits and prices by jurisdiction; registers of approved clinical AI products; records of licensed autonomous transport services.
counts_against: Outcomes follow AI adoption and not the rules: jurisdictions with similar adoption and different rules show similar entry and prices, while jurisdictions with similar rules and different adoption diverge.
does_not_count: Evidence from one sector only. The prediction is about the institutional layer as a whole.

measure: Share of new AI infrastructure (data-center capacity, chip fabrication capacity) and of net high-skilled migration that goes to jurisdictions ranked in the top third by a standard index of state capacity at the baseline.
public_sources: Industry and government reports on data-center and fab capacity by country; migration statistics; a published governance index, fixed at its baseline values.
counts_against: The share going to the top third is lower at the final reading than at the 2026 baseline: infrastructure and talent dispersed toward weaker-capacity jurisdictions.
does_not_count: Capacity built in a weaker-capacity jurisdiction but owned and controlled from a high-capacity one. The reading must separate where capacity stands from who controls it.

measure: Cost of the reference bundle (shelter, energy, basic health care, basic mobility, connectivity) as a share of the disposable income of the lowest income fifth of households, set beside a price index for AI-mediated services. Recorded with it: the share of transfers in the income of that group, and its asset holdings.
public_sources: Household budget surveys; consumer price indices by category; published prices of AI services.
counts_against: In most of the economies examined, the bundle's share of income falls for the lowest fifth while the price of AI services falls, without a rise in the share of transfers in their income and without broader asset holdings: cost compression alone reached households.
does_not_count: A fall in the bundle's share that comes with higher transfers or broader household claims. That is the route the paper itself names, so it does not count against the paper.

measure: Change in operating margin from each baseline to each reading, airport slot and gate holders and hub operators minus airline carriers.
public_sources: Company annual reports; airport and airline industry statistics.
counts_against: The difference is negative at the final reading: carriers gained relative to the holders of airport capacity.
does_not_count: A single year. Margins in this industry swing with fuel prices and demand shocks, so the baselines and the readings are averages of three years. Where a carrier holds its own slots, it is classed as a carrier.

measure: Change in operating margin (or revenue per available room net of costs) from each baseline to each reading, prime-location and strong-brand hotels minus undifferentiated mid-market hotels.
public_sources: Company annual reports; hotel industry statistics by segment.
counts_against: The difference is negative at the final reading: mid-market inventory gained relative to prime locations and strong brands.
does_not_count: A single year, for the same reason as T7: the baselines and the readings are averages of three years.

measure: Change in operating margin from each baseline to each reading, integrated logistics networks and port operators minus commoditized carriers.
public_sources: Company annual reports; port and shipping industry statistics.
counts_against: The difference is negative at the final reading: commoditized carriers gained relative to integrated networks and ports.
does_not_count: A single year. Freight rates are strongly cyclical, so the baselines and the readings are averages of three years.

measure: Change in net operating income per unit of floor area, and in occupancy, from each baseline to each reading: data-center and logistics real estate trusts minus generic office trusts.
public_sources: Annual reports of listed real estate trusts; commercial property statistics.
counts_against: The difference is negative at the final reading: generic offices gained relative to data centers and logistics property.
does_not_count: Share prices of the trusts. They move with interest rates and expectations; the prediction is about rents. The baselines and the readings are averages of three years.

measure: Change in operating margin from each baseline to each reading, hyperscale cloud and AI platforms minus software product firms without proprietary infrastructure.
public_sources: Company annual reports and segment disclosures.
counts_against: The difference is negative at the final reading: software product firms without infrastructure gained relative to the platforms.
does_not_count: Firms that changed group during the period, for example by building their own infrastructure. The article treats exposure as something actors can change, so each firm is classified at the baseline and reclassifications are reported. This pairing is the record's own: unlike T7 to T10 it sets a row of Panel C against a row of Panel A, not against its counterpart in Panel E.
